about.text: Blue cheese is any cheese made with the addition of cultures of edible molds, which create blue-green spots or veins through the cheese. Blue cheeses vary in flavor from mild to strong and from slightly sweet to salty or sharp; in color from pale to dark; and in consistency from liquid to hard. They may have a distinctive smell, either from the mold or from various specially cultivated bacteria such as Brevibacterium linens.

picks.why: The archetypal blue, a PDO sheep's-milk cheese ripened in Combalou caves and famed since the Middle Ages.
Italy's defining blue, a PDO cow's-milk cheese dating back centuries and eaten and exported worldwide.
England's king of blues, a PDO cheese made in only three counties and a Christmas staple.
Denmark's mild, salty Danablu, a PGI cheese created in 1927 and exported across the world.
Spain's most famous blue, a strong PDO cheese ripened in Asturian mountain caves.
